trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Disney World, Orlando, Florida
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight arrives late night
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight arrives late night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Take the Ramada free theme park shuttle or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber ~$25-30) to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and review your Disney World park tickets and plans for the week. Download the My Disney Experience app if not already done.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from the hotel vending machine or a nearby 24-hour Walmart Supercenter (~1.5 miles away on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy) to stock up on breakfast items and snacks for the week

day_by_day.notes: Pro tip: Stop at Walmart or Publix near the hotel to buy bottled water, granola bars, fruit, and easy breakfast items to save significant money throughout the week. Disney allows you to bring in outside food and non-alcoholic beverages. Pack a small backpack cooler each day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after late arrival. Enjoy a self-prepared breakfast in the hotel room. Head to Magic Kingdom via the free hotel shuttle (confirm shuttle schedule at front desk the night before). Arrive at park opening (typically 9:00 AM). Use the My Disney Experience app to grab Lightning Lane selections for top rides. Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain and then Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Ride Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Watch the Festival of Fantasy parade (check app for times). Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed (use the free shuttle) to rest and avoid peak heat and crowds, then return for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for the evening. Experience rides with shorter wait times after 7 PM. Watch the spectacular Happily Ever After fireworks show (typically at 9:00 PM). Take the free shuttle back to the hotel afterward.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared in hotel room (items purchased from Walmart the night before) - granola bars, fruit, yogurt cups
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square - budget-friendly counter service with clam chowder, sandwiches, and fish & chips (~$12-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland - one of Magic Kingdom's best counter service spots with burgers, rotisserie chicken, and salads (~$13-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and apply sunscreen generously - June in Orlando is hot and humid (expect 90°F+). Bring a refillable water bottle; free water is available at any quick-service restaurant. Purchase a Disney Dining Plan in advance or use the Disney gift card strategy to budget meals. Arrive at the park 30 minutes before official opening for 'rope drop' advantage.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to EPCOT, arriving at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Head immediately to Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane required - set an alarm for 7:00 AM to grab a boarding group via the app). Then ride Test Track and Soarin' Around the World before lines grow. Explore Future World East and West pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk around the World Showcase, which opens at 11:00 AM. Explore international pavilions including Mexico, Norway (ride Frozen Ever After), China, Japan, and France. Sample affordable international snacks and street food from various pavilions as a budget-friendly way to 'eat around the world' (~$5-8 per snack item). Visit the Canada and UK pavilions.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's Harmonious nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check app for show times, typically 9:00 PM). This is one of the largest nighttime shows Disney has ever created. Take the free hotel shuttle back after the show.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel room breakfast - instant oatmeal, fruit, and coffee/juice
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion - excellent value counter service with rotisserie chicken, sandwiches, and Asian-inspired dishes (~$12-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Graze on international snacks around World Showcase for a fun and budget-friendly dinner experience: School Bread from Norway (~$5), Tacos from Mexico (~$8), and a crepe from France (~$7) - total ~$20 per person

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the most walkable park - wear extra comfortable shoes. The World Showcase is perfect for families who enjoy culture and food. Check the EPCOT app for any special festivals happening (Flower & Garden Festival runs spring, Food & Wine Festival runs fall) which may add extra entertainment. Free water is available at any quick-service location.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios, arriving at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). This is the most competitive park for Lightning Lane - book Tiana's Bayou Adventure or Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance first thing. Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge. Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run (shorter wait than Rise of the Resistance). Then rush to Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toy Story Land fully - ride Alien Swirling Saucers and enjoy the theming. Head to Sunset Boulevard for Rock 'n' Roller Coaster and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. Watch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show times). Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel to cool off and rest (use free shuttle), then return refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hollywood Studios for the evening. Watch the Fantasmic! nighttime show (check app for times and arrive 45-60 minutes early for good seating). Experience any remaining rides with shorter evening wait times. Take the free hotel shuttle back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel room breakfast - cereal, milk, and fruit
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land - fan-favorite counter service with totchos, grilled cheese sandwiches, and lunch box tarts (~$10-14 per person). Arrive early or late to avoid peak lines.
meals.dinner: Backlot Express near Echo Lake - burgers, chicken strips, and salads at some of the most affordable prices in Hollywood Studios (~$11-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most thrill-ride-heavy park - not ideal for very young children but great for older kids and adults. The Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge land is incredibly immersive. Consider building a lightsaber at Savi's Workshop (~$249) or a droid at Droid Depot (~$119) if budget allows as a special splurge. Grab a Blue or Green Milk from the Milk Stand for a unique Star Wars experience (~$7).

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom, arriving at rope drop (typically 8:00 AM - Animal Kingdom often opens earliest). Head directly to Pandora - The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage first (longest waits in the park) then Na'vi River Journey. The early morning light in Pandora is absolutely magical. Then head to Africa for Kilimanjaro Safaris - morning is the best time as animals are most active.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Discovery Island and Asia. Ride Expedition Everest in Asia (great thrill coaster). Watch the Festival of the Lion King show in Africa (check times - one of Disney's best live shows). Walk the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for free wildlife viewing. Visit the Tree of Life and look for the hidden animals carved into its trunk.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for Rivers of Light nighttime show or Tree of Life Awakenings (check app for current evening entertainment as programming changes). Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks (~8:00-9:00 PM). Head back to the hotel via free shuttle and enjoy a relaxing evening. Consider a swim in the hotel pool.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel room breakfast - grab-and-go items like bananas, granola bars, and juice boxes
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue on Discovery Island - one of the best counter service meals in all of Disney World with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken with beautiful outdoor waterfront seating (~$14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora - The World of Avatar - healthy and delicious bowls with rice, noodles, or greens topped with protein choices (~$13-16 per person). Unique and flavorful food in a stunning setting.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning when animals are active and temperatures are cooler. Bring bug spray as the park has more outdoor areas. The Pandora land is breathtaking - especially at night when the bioluminescent plants glow. This is a great day for families with younger children as the park has many gentle experiences alongside thrills.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning - sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. This is your resort/rest day. Enjoy the Ramada hotel pool. Walk or take a short rideshare to Old Town Kissimmee (about 1 mile away) - a free outdoor entertainment complex with shops, restaurants, and weekly car shows. Browse the shops and enjoy the retro Florida atmosphere at no cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Icon Park on International Drive (about 8 miles from hotel - take a rideshare ~$12-15 each way). Explore the free outdoor entertainment district with restaurants and shops. Consider the free-to-browse areas. Alternatively, visit the Kissimmee Lakefront Park (free admission) for a relaxing afternoon by the lake with playgrounds and walking paths. Or use this afternoon for a second visit to your favorite Disney park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Disney Springs (free admission, free parking) via rideshare or hotel shuttle if offered. Disney Springs is Disney's massive outdoor shopping, dining, and entertainment complex. Enjoy live music, browse unique shops, watch street performers, and soak in the atmosphere completely free. Have dinner at one of the many restaurant options ranging from budget to upscale.

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast if included, or self-prepared room breakfast
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at Old Town Kissimmee or a local Kissimmee restaurant - try Azteca D'Oro Mexican Restaurant nearby for authentic and affordable Mexican food (~$8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Disney Springs dining - Chicken Guy! by Guy Fieri for affordable chicken tenders and sandwiches (~$10-13 per person), or grab food from multiple quick-service spots for a fun variety meal

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day at Disney parks - this is intentionally scheduled as your off-park day to avoid the largest crowds. Disney Springs is completely free to enter and offers a full evening of entertainment without park admission. The Boathouse, STK, and other upscale restaurants at Disney Springs are splurge options if budget allows. Live music at various venues throughout Disney Springs is free.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 11:00 AM - request late checkout if your flight allows). Enjoy a final self-prepared breakfast or grab a quick meal nearby. If time permits before checkout, take one last dip in the hotel pool. Pack carefully and ensure all souvenirs are secured. Store luggage with the hotel front desk if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: If flight is in the late afternoon or evening, consider a final few hours at Disney Springs (free admission) for last-minute souvenir shopping and a farewell lunch. Alternatively, visit a nearby outlet mall - Orlando Premium Outlets on Vineland Avenue (~5 miles away) for discounted Disney merchandise and other shopping. Take the hotel shuttle or rideshare to Orlando International Airport (~25-30 minutes, rideshare ~$25-35).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Orlando International Airport. Arrive at least 2 hours before domestic flight or 3 hours before international flight. Reflect on an amazing week at Disney World!

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining hotel room food supplies - finish any snacks, fruit, and drinks purchased earlier in the week
meals.lunch: Disney Springs quick service for a final Disney meal, or grab lunch at Orlando International Airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Before leaving, check if the hotel offers a free shuttle to the airport - if not, book a rideshare in advance. Orlando International Airport has good food options post-security. Consider purchasing any remaining Disney souvenirs at Disney Springs rather than inside the parks where prices are identical but the atmosphere is more relaxed. Don't forget to check all hotel room drawers, bathroom, and safe before departing. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and hotel): Park tickets ~$400-600 per adult for 4-day ticket, meals ~$40-60/day per person using counter service and room snacks, extras ~$50-100 for souvenirs and transportation.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Take the hotel's free theme park shuttle or a rideshare to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and review your Disney park tickets and plans for the week. Grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or the hotel vending area.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night snack upon arrival – grab quick bites from a nearby Walgreens, 7-Eleven, or a late-night fast food spot like McDonald's or Taco Bell on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (open 24 hours, within 1 mile of hotel).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – rest is essential after a late arrival. Set alarms early for Day 2. Download the My Disney Experience app if not already done, link your park tickets, and set up Lightning Lane preferences. Confirm the hotel shuttle schedule for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day Adventure – Start early with the hotel's free theme park shuttle (aim for the first shuttle, typically around 7:30–8:00 AM). Arrive at Magic Kingdom before park opening (rope drop around 9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train. Use Lightning Lane for high-demand rides. Explore Cinderella Castle and Main Street U.S.A. in the cooler morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom – tackle Big Thunder Mountain Railroad in Frontierland, Pirates of the Caribbean, and the Haunted Mansion. Take a midday break (1:00–3:00 PM) to escape the Florida heat at a sit-down restaurant or air-conditioned attraction like the Hall of Presidents or Mickey's PhilharMagic. Return refreshed for afternoon rides with shorter wait times.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Magic Kingdom nighttime spectacular – the 'Disney Enchantment' fireworks show (typically at 9:00 PM). Grab a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. about 30–45 minutes early. Catch the electrical parade if scheduled. Take the hotel shuttle back after the show.

meals.breakfast: Quick-service breakfast at the hotel or grab a pastry and coffee at The Main Street Bakery (Starbucks) inside Magic Kingdom – budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square – excellent mid-range quick-service option with clam chowder, fish and chips, and chicken sandwiches. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A. – a classic, affordable table-service option with sandwiches, salads, and milkshakes. Make an ADV (Advance Dining Reservation) via My Disney Experience. Budget ~$20–$30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen – June in Orlando is hot and humid (highs around 90°F/32°C). Stay hydrated; free water cups are available at any quick-service location. Purchase a refillable resort mug if you plan to use hotel dining. Lightning Lane Multi Pass is recommended for Magic Kingdom.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Experience – Take the hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios for rope drop. Head directly to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge. Book a Savi's Workshop lightsaber-building experience (reserve in advance – ~$249.99 per lightsaber, worth it for Star Wars fans) or visit the Droid Depot to build a custom droid (~$119.99). Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first thing to avoid long waits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ride Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance (use Lightning Lane Individual – book at 7:00 AM on the day). Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios – ride Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land, Rock 'n' Roller Coaster, and Tower of Terror. Take a midday break at the hotel or in an air-conditioned show like Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Hollywood Studios nighttime show – 'Fantasmic!' (check schedule, typically 8:00 or 9:00 PM). Arrive 45 minutes early for good seats. Alternatively, catch the 'Star Wars: A Galactic Spectacular' fireworks if scheduled. Head back to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel's complimentary continental breakfast (if available) or stop at a Denny's or IHOP near the hotel on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy – budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge – themed quick-service with unique dishes like Smoked Kaadu Ribs and Fried Endorian Tip-Yip. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – a beloved Hollywood Studios table-service restaurant where you dine in retro cars watching classic sci-fi movie clips. Make an ADR in advance. Budget ~$25–$35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop and Droid Depot require advance reservations – book as early as possible (60 days out for resort guests). If budget is a concern, skip the experiences and focus on rides. Rise of the Resistance is the must-do attraction; secure a Lightning Lane Individual purchase at exactly 7:00 AM. Bring ponchos – afternoon thunderstorms are common in June.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT for rope drop. Start in Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature) – ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane Individual – join at park open), Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France Pavilion, and Test Track. Explore the stunning new World Nature area with Living with the Land boat ride.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the World Showcase Food & Culture Tour starting at 12:00 PM when most pavilions fully open. Walk the World Showcase Lagoon and sample food and drinks from pavilions: Mexico (churros, margaritas), Japan (sushi, mochi), Morocco (hummus, baklava), France (crêpes, macarons), and more. Explore the cultural exhibits, artisan shops, and live entertainment in each pavilion. Ride Frozen Ever After in Norway.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's 'EPCOT Forever' or 'Harmonious' nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check current show schedule – typically 9:00 PM). Find a spot around the lagoon about 30–40 minutes early. Take the shuttle back to the hotel after the show.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons in The Land Pavilion – EPCOT's best quick-service breakfast with fresh options. Budget ~$12–$18 per person.
meals.lunch: World Showcase food booths and kiosks – graze through multiple countries sampling small plates and drinks. Budget ~$25–$35 per person for a satisfying tour of flavors.
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion – a fun, interactive teppanyaki table-service experience. Make an ADR in advance. Budget ~$30–$45 per person. Alternatively, La Hacienda de San Angel in Mexico for a lakeside dinner with great views.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the most 'adult-friendly' park but kids love Remy's Ratatouille Adventure and Frozen Ever After. The World Showcase doesn't fully open until 11:00 AM, so use the morning for Future World attractions. Comfortable walking shoes are essential – EPCOT is one of the largest parks to walk. Consider renting a stroller for young children.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience – Take the hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom for rope drop. Head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride – use Lightning Lane Individual, purchased at 7:00 AM). The queue theming alone is spectacular. Ride Na'vi River Journey afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Africa for the Kilimanjaro Safaris – aim for an early afternoon ride when animals are more active (avoid midday heat). See lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and more on this 20-minute open-air safari. Explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail on foot. Visit Asia for Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (you WILL get wet – great for the heat!). Check out the Tree of Life and 'It's Tough to Be a Bug!' show.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the 'Rivers of Light' nighttime show or 'Tree of Life Awakenings' (check current schedule – Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks, typically 8:00–9:00 PM). Enjoy a relaxed dinner before heading back to the hotel for an earlier night.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the hotel or a quick stop at a nearby Cracker Barrel on US-192 – a great mid-range family breakfast option. Budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora – Animal Kingdom's best quick-service restaurant with healthy, flavorful bowls and unique drinks. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia – a popular table-service restaurant with Asian-fusion cuisine in a beautifully themed setting. Make an ADR. Budget ~$25–$35 per person. Alternatively, Flame Tree Barbecue for a more budget-friendly quick-service option with outdoor waterfront seating.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning and late afternoon – midday heat can be intense and many animals rest during peak heat. Bring a change of clothes or a poncho for Kali River Rapids. Flight of Passage is the #1 must-do at this park – securing a Lightning Lane Individual at 7:00 AM is highly recommended. The park typically closes earlier than others, so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and Recovery / Hotel Pool Morning – After five busy days, take a well-deserved slow morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend time at the hotel pool. The Ramada Kissimmee Gateway has pool facilities – a great way to relax and recharge. Alternatively, explore the International Drive area or visit a nearby outlet mall (Orlando Premium Outlets is about 15 minutes away) for some souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Afternoon – Take the hotel shuttle or a rideshare to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required). Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Visit the LEGO Store, World of Disney (largest Disney merchandise store), and unique boutiques. Check out the Splitsville Luxury Lanes bowling alley or catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater. Kids will love the LEGO fountain play area.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Evening – Enjoy live entertainment from street performers and musicians throughout Disney Springs. Browse the unique dining options and entertainment venues. Consider the Cirque du Soleil 'Drawn to Life' show (book tickets in advance – ~$75–$114 per person) for a spectacular family entertainment experience. Explore the waterfront area as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a nearby Perkins Restaurant & Bakery on US-192 – a classic family breakfast spot. Budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs – gourmet burgers, hand-cut fries, and milkshakes in a quick-service setting. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs – a waterfront table-service restaurant with fresh seafood, steaks, and classic American fare. A mid-range splurge for a special evening. Make an ADR. Budget ~$35–$55 per person. Alternatively, Rainforest Cafe for a more family-friendly, budget-conscious option (~$20–$30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a great way to enjoy Disney magic without a park ticket. Parking is free in the Disney Springs garages. The hotel shuttle may not serve Disney Springs directly – check with the front desk or use a rideshare (Uber/Lyft, ~$10–$15 each way). Saturday evenings at Disney Springs can be very crowded – arrive by 5:00 PM to secure a good dinner reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom or EPCOT Revisit (Choose Your Favorite) – Use your final full park day to revisit your favorite park or catch any rides you missed. Magic Kingdom is ideal for a final morning with a more relaxed pace – enjoy the rides you loved again, pick up last-minute souvenirs on Main Street U.S.A., and soak in the atmosphere. Alternatively, return to EPCOT for any World Showcase pavilions or Future World attractions you didn't get to.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Park Exploration and Souvenir Shopping – Spend the afternoon enjoying your chosen park at a leisurely pace. Visit any remaining attractions, take photos at iconic spots (Cinderella Castle, Spaceship Earth), and do your final souvenir shopping. World of Disney at Disney Springs or the park's own gift shops are great options. Head back to the hotel by 4:00–5:00 PM to begin packing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner near the Hotel – Enjoy a relaxed farewell dinner at one of the many restaurants along W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy or US-192 near the hotel. Pack your bags, confirm your departure transportation, and reflect on an amazing week at Disney World. Get a good night's sleep before your departure.

meals.breakfast: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Magic Kingdom (if revisiting) – a magical table-service breakfast inside the Beast's Castle. Make an ADR well in advance. Budget ~$25–$35 per person. Or a quick continental breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Quick-service lunch at your chosen park – Casey's Corner (hot dogs) or Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café at Magic Kingdom, or Sunshine Seasons at EPCOT. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Olive Garden or LongHorn Steakhouse on US-192 near the hotel – reliable, mid-range family dining with generous portions. Budget ~$20–$30 per person. Or treat yourself to a final Disney meal at a park restaurant if you stay for the evening.

day_by_day.notes: Check your hotel's checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. Confirm your return transportation to Orlando International Airport in advance – the hotel shuttle may not serve the airport, so book a rideshare or shuttle service (Mears Connect or Sunshine Flyer, ~$16–$25 per person). Leave extra time for airport security, especially during peak summer travel. Don't forget to check for any forgotten items in the hotel room safe, pool area, or shuttle!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Disney World, Orlando, Florida Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

experiences.description: Spend a full day at the iconic Magic Kingdom, riding classics like Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and the Haunted Mansion. Watch the Festival of Fantasy parade and end the night with the spectacular Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (arrive at rope drop) through Evening

experiences.name: Hollywood Studios Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Experience
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the Star Wars universe at Galaxy's Edge. Build your own lightsaber at Savi's Workshop, pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, and experience the thrilling Rise of the Resistance ride. Enjoy themed food and drinks at Oga's Cantina.
experiences.location: Hollywood Studios, Galaxy's Edge, Walt Disney World Resort

experiences.description: Explore EPCOT's World Showcase, sampling authentic cuisine and experiencing cultural pavilions from 11 countries including France, Japan, Morocco, and Mexico. experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience

Then journey to Pandora – The World of Avatar for the breathtaking Flight of Passage ride and the magical Na'vi River Journey, especially stunning after dark when bioluminescent plants glow.

experiences.location: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Pandora – The World of Avatar, Walt Disney World Resort

experiences.name: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Evening
experiences.description: Spend a fun-filled evening at Disney Springs exploring unique shops, world-class dining, and live entertainment. Enjoy dinner at The BOATHOUSE or T-REX Cafe, catch a show at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater, and let kids experience the interactive fountain play area. No park ticket required.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and recovery only.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and recovery only.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the hotel's complimentary theme park shuttle or a pre-booked luxury car service (recommend Mears Connect Black or a private car) to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Grab a light late-night snack from the hotel's amenities or a nearby 24-hour spot.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night arrival — grab a light bite at the hotel's lobby bar or order room service if available. Alternatively, Denny's (open 24 hrs, 2 min drive) for a casual late-night meal.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is after 10 PM. Purchase Disney Park tickets and make dining reservations (via My Disney Experience app) before the trip — top restaurants book 60 days in advance. Download the My Disney Experience app and link your tickets tonight if energy allows.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Head to Magic Kingdom Park for a Full Day Adventure. Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM) via the hotel's free theme park shuttle. Start with the most popular rides using Lightning Lane Multi Pass: Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train. Explore Fantasyland and Tomorrowland in the cooler morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Enjoy the Festival of Fantasy Parade (typically ~3:00 PM). Ride Haunted Mansion, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Splash Mountain. Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed (shuttle runs regularly) to rest and freshen up before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for the spectacular Happily Ever After fireworks show (typically ~9:00 PM). Stake out a premium viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. at least 45 minutes early. Enjoy the magical atmosphere of the park lit up at night before heading back to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A. (Magic Kingdom) — elegant Victorian-style dining with classic American breakfast. Reservation recommended.
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Magic Kingdom, Fantasyland) — dine inside the Beast's enchanted castle. Prix-fixe lunch menu with French-inspired cuisine in a stunning setting. Reservation essential.
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table (Magic Kingdom) — a once-in-a-lifetime premium dining experience inside Cinderella Castle. Multi-course dinner with character meet-and-greets. Book 60 days in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Lightning Lane Multi Pass ($25–$35/person/day) and individual Lightning Lane selections for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and Tron Lightcycle Run to minimize wait times. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen — June in Orlando is hot and humid (expect 90°F+). Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hollywood Studios for the Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Experience. Arrive early to secure a boarding group or Lightning Lane for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance (one of Disney's most immersive rides). Begin your morning in Galaxy's Edge — explore Black Spire Outpost, interact with roaming characters like Rey and Kylo Ren, and pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Savi's Workshop to build a custom lightsaber — a premium, deeply immersive experience ($299.99/lightsaber, reservations required). Afterward, explore the rest of Hollywood Studios: ride Slinky Dog Dash, Tower of Terror, and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Fantasmic! nighttime spectacular at Hollywood Studios — an epic outdoor show featuring Mickey Mouse, Disney villains, and stunning water/fire/projection effects. Arrive 45–60 minutes early for premium seating. Head back to the hotel via shuttle and wind down with a drink at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo (Galaxy's Edge, Hollywood Studios) — themed Star Wars breakfast in an immersive setting. Try the Ronto-less Garden Wrap or Mustafarian Lard Rolls.
meals.lunch: Oga's Cantina (Galaxy's Edge, Hollywood Studios) — the most exclusive bar/lounge in Star Wars land. Enjoy themed cocktails, non-alcoholic drinks, and light bites in an incredibly atmospheric setting. Reservations are a must.
meals.dinner: The Hollywood Brown Derby (Hollywood Studios) — a recreation of the legendary 1930s Hollywood restaurant. Upscale American cuisine with signature Cobb Salad prepared tableside. A true premium dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop reservations must be made well in advance — book as soon as your 60-day window opens. Oga's Cantina has a 45-minute time limit per visit and requires reservations. Consider the Fantasmic! Dining Package which includes a reserved viewing area for the show bundled with a restaurant meal.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning — sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and take advantage of the hotel pool or spa facilities. This is a planned rest day to recharge mid-trip. Use the morning to review upcoming park plans, make any last-minute dining reservations, and browse the My Disney Experience app for Lightning Lane availability.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Disney Springs for the Family Entertainment Experience. Arrive early afternoon to explore the vibrant waterfront shopping and entertainment district. Visit unique shops like World of Disney (the largest Disney merchandise store in the world), LEGO Store, and Marketplace Co-Op. Enjoy live entertainment from street performers and musicians throughout the district.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening at Disney Springs enjoying world-class dining and entertainment. Catch a show at the AMC Disney Springs 24 Theatre or enjoy the Cirque du Soleil Drawn to Life show — a breathtaking acrobatic performance inspired by Disney animation (tickets ~$75–$175/person). Stroll the waterfront promenade before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby Keke's Breakfast Cafe (Kissimmee) — a beloved local brunch spot with extensive menu options.
meals.lunch: Morimoto Asia (Disney Springs) — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship restaurant featuring pan-Asian cuisine in a stunning two-story space. Try the Peking Duck or sushi platters.
meals.dinner: STK Orlando (Disney Springs) — a modern, upscale steakhouse with a lively atmosphere. Premium USDA cuts, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine list. One of the finest dining experiences in the Disney Springs area.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter — no park ticket required. Cirque du Soleil Drawn to Life tickets should be booked in advance. This mid-trip rest day is strategically placed to prevent theme park fatigue, especially important for families with children. Disney Springs is easily accessible via the hotel's free shuttle.

day_by_day.morning: Head to EPCOT for the World Showcase Food & Culture Tour. Arrive at park opening and start with Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature). Ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (book Individual Lightning Lane immediately upon park entry), Remy's Ratatouille Adventure, and Test Track. Explore the stunning new World Nature pavilion featuring the Living with the Land boat ride.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase as it opens at 11:00 AM. Embark on a self-guided food and culture tour around the 11 international pavilions. Sample authentic cuisine and beverages from Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Participate in cultural experiences, watch traditional performances, and browse artisan shops in each pavilion.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's spectacular EPCOT Forever or Harmonious nighttime show over World Showcase Lagoon — one of the largest nighttime spectaculars ever created. Secure a premium viewing spot along the lagoon promenade. Enjoy a final evening drink at La Cava del Tequila (Mexico Pavilion) before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons (EPCOT, The Land Pavilion) — a quick-service option with fresh, healthy options including grain bowls, sandwiches, and pastries. Great for a quick start before the park gets busy.
meals.lunch: Teppan Edo (EPCOT, Japan Pavilion) — an authentic Japanese teppanyaki experience where skilled chefs prepare your meal tableside with theatrical flair. Stunning views of World Showcase Lagoon.
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul (EPCOT, France Pavilion) — EPCOT's most upscale restaurant, located above the France Pavilion. Classic French haute cuisine with an extensive wine list and panoramic lagoon views. A true fine-dining gem inside a theme park.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase is a food lover's paradise — budget extra for food and drink tastings across pavilions (plan $15–$30 per person per pavilion stop). The EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival runs seasonally and may offer additional tasting booths if active during your visit. Monsieur Paul requires reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Disney's Animal Kingdom for the Safari & Avatar Experience. Arrive at rope drop — Animal Kingdom opens early (often 8:00 AM) and wildlife is most active in the cooler morning hours. Begin immediately with Kilimanjaro Safaris — a 20-minute open-vehicle safari through a stunning 110-acre savanna featuring lions, elephants, giraffes, rhinos, hippos, and more. Follow with the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Journey to Pandora — The World of Avatar for an awe-inspiring afternoon. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage (book Lightning Lane first thing — this is the most in-demand ride at Animal Kingdom) — a breathtaking banshee-riding simulator over the alien moon of Pandora. Explore the bioluminescent landscape of the Valley of Mo'ara and ride Na'vi River Journey. Visit the Tree of Life and watch the 'It's Tough to Be a Bug!' 4D show.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Rivers of Light: We Are One — Animal Kingdom's nighttime spectacular featuring floating lanterns, water screens, and animal imagery. Afterward, enjoy a final magical evening stroll through Discovery Island before heading back to the hotel for a relaxing night.

meals.breakfast: Tusker House Restaurant (Animal Kingdom, Africa) — a character dining experience featuring Donald Duck, Daisy, Mickey, and Goofy in safari attire. Buffet-style African-inspired breakfast with unique flavors. Reservations essential.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen (Animal Kingdom, Pandora) — the best quick-service restaurant in Animal Kingdom. Customizable bowls with unique proteins and bases inspired by Pandoran cuisine. Healthy, fresh, and delicious.
meals.dinner: Tiffins Restaurant (Animal Kingdom) — Disney's most sophisticated Animal Kingdom dining experience. Globally-inspired cuisine celebrating the art of travel and exploration. Stunning artwork, intimate atmosphere, and an exceptional wine and cocktail program. A must for luxury travelers.

day_by_day.notes: Book Avatar Flight of Passage Lightning Lane as your very first action upon park entry — it sells out within minutes. Kilimanjaro Safaris is best experienced at park opening when animals are most active. Tiffins is one of Disney's hidden gem fine-dining restaurants and is often easier to book than Magic Kingdom's top spots — still reserve 60 days out.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely, luxurious breakfast and begin packing. Check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 11:00 AM — request late checkout if your flight allows). Take one last stroll or pool dip if time permits. Reflect on the magical week with your family over a special breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, consider a final visit to Disney Springs for last-minute souvenir shopping at World of Disney, or revisit a favorite park for a few final rides using any remaining Lightning Lane credits. Alternatively, explore the Kissimmee/Orlando area — visit ICON Park on International Drive for the Orlando Eye observation wheel or a final premium lunch before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Orlando International Airport via pre-booked luxury car service or hotel shuttle. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and boarding. Reflect on an unforgettable week of Disney magic as you depart Orlando.

meals.breakfast: Chef Art Smith's Homecomin' (Disney Springs) — a farewell Southern comfort food breakfast by celebrity chef Art Smith. Famous for fried chicken, biscuits, and indulgent Southern classics. A warm, memorable final meal.
meals.lunch: The Boathouse (Disney Springs) — upscale waterfront dining featuring fresh seafood, prime steaks, and stunning views of the Disney Springs waterway. Perfect for a relaxed final lunch with the family.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Orlando International Airport — MSY has several solid options in the terminal, or enjoy a meal before departing at a nearby restaurant on International Drive.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and arrange airport transportation the night before. If you have a late evening flight, Disney Springs is the perfect final destination as it requires no park ticket and the hotel shuttle services it. Consider purchasing a Disney gift card or personalized keepsakes as lasting mementos. Tip: Download all your Disney PhotoPass photos before leaving — they expire 45 days after your last park visit.
